metadata.title: PISA science framework 2018 vs 2025 and its impact in physics education: Literature review

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This paper is a descriptive literature review (SLR) combined with bibliometric analysis, not an analysis of student microdata from PISA. Therefore, there is no sampling frame of students/schools and no application of PISA sampling weights or replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife). The study does not generate or scale achievement scores (PVs) from respondents; instead, it synthesizes and maps the conceptual structure of the PISA science frameworks (2018/2015–2018 vs 2025). As a result, weighting variables from PISA databases are not relevant to the reported findings.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because the study does not estimate or model PISA achievement outcomes from student responses; it compares framework components (contexts, knowledge, competencies, and science identity) and summarizes literature trends. Missing-data handling is not reported because there is no respondent-level dataset with item nonresponse or PV generation; the analysis is based on article collection and bibliometric visualization rather than statistical estimation on microdata.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used a systematic literature review (SLR) approach with bibliometric analysis. Articles were collected from Google Scholar and Scopus using keywords related to 'PISA Science Framework', 'Science Literacy', or combinations thereof; the paper does not report an analytic student sample because it does not analyze PISA microdata.

data.outcome_summary: This article compares the PISA science literacy framework used in 2018 (building on the 2015 science literacy structure) with the newer PISA 2025 science framework through a systematic literature review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis. Rather than estimating student achievement, it synthesizes how the framework’s components change: PISA 2018 is organized around contexts, competencies, and knowledge (including procedural and epistemic knowledge), while PISA 2025 reorganizes competencies and adds science identity (science capital/epistemic beliefs, attitudes/dispositions, and environmental awareness/agency). The bibliometric network visualizations (e.g., VOSviewer) are used to identify clusters and research trends linking scientific literacy, nature of science, and physics learning. The study’s implication is curricular and instructional: physics education should align learning activities with the 2025 emphasis on applying scientific information for decision-making and action, while also supporting inquiry design and critical interpretation of evidence.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction contains no student-level sample sizes, PV handling, missing-data strategy, or ML model evaluation because the paper is a literature review and bibliometric mapping rather than an empirical predictive/causal analysis of PISA microdata. Consequently, fields such as total_students, countries, and main_findings (structured predictive outcomes) are intentionally empty.
